full_judgment:
Abdul Matin Khan Chowdhury, J.—This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause why the order dated 16 5.84 allowing the decree holder to realise interest and order dated 20 5.84 refusing to withdraw attachment orders passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Narayanganj in Money Execution Case No 12 of 1983 should not be set aside. 

 2. It appears that the plaintiff filed the suit for recovery of Tk. 50,226 70 from the petitioner. It further appears that at the time of hearing the defendant-petitioners admitted the claim of the plaintiff and in pursuance of that admission the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit on admission with costs. As per the said judgment and decree dated 13.3.81 the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 started Execution case No. 12, of 1983 for the realisation of the decretal amount along with interest and the properties of the petitioner which has been attached was going to be sold in auction. Whereupon the petitioner filed an application before the Execution Court for exemption of interest in the decretal amount. The learned Subordinate Judge as per his orders dated 16 5.84 and 20 5.84 rejected the prayer for exemption. Being aggrieved the petitioner filed an application u/s. 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained this rule. 

 3. Mr. Md. Nurul Huq, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that as there was no decree passed in the matter in respect of interest against the petitioner, as such the opposite party No. 1 is not entitled to execute the decree claiming interest on the decretal amount. He further submits that the decree in question does not specifically show that the interest has been decreed. As such according to him, the plaintiff-opposite party is not entitled to realise any interest on the claimed amount. 

 4. Mr. Asrarul Hossain, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite party No. 1, submits that the decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge was on admission which includes the entire claim of the plaintiff opposite party No. 1 along with interest at the rate of 13% on the claimed amount till the realisation of the dues. He further submits that as the decree has been passed on admission, as such it does not require to mention in the judgment about the interest, because of the fact that the plaint itself shows that interest has been claimed by the plaintiff in the plaint and that has been decreed on admission. 

 5. It appears from the plaint that the plaintiff filed the suit for a decree for recovery of Tk. 50, 226 70 as described in the schedule of the plaint with interest at the rate of 13% till the date of realisation of the same. It appears from the judgment passed by the learned Subordinate Judge on 31.3 83 that the learned Subordinate Judge decreed the suit on admission with costs. This clearly shows that the entire amount as claimed on the plaint together with the interest at the rate of 13% was decreed. As such there is no scope for exemption of payment of interest as prayed by the petitioner. 

 7. Mr. Asrarul Hossain, learned Advocate has cited a decision reported in A.I.R. 1926 Sind 119 wherein it has been held that it was not necessary to have a decree drawn up on a judgment obtained on admission under Order 12, rule 6. It is open to the plaintiff to en-force payment of the amount awarded as an order in execution proceedings by virtue of section 36. It was further held in that case none a judgment OD admission decree need not be drawn up. Plaintiff may enforce payment of the amount awarded as an order in execution by reasons of title Suit". 

 8. From the above quotation it is apparent that if a judgment has been passed on admission then no decree need be drawn up and the plaintiff may enforce payment of the decree in pursuance of the judgment. In the instant case, we find that the decree has been passed on admission which includes an interest at the rate of 13% till the date of realisation of the due. In this view of the matter, we do not find any substance in the argument advanced by the learned Advocate for the petitioner. 

 9. Mr. Asrarul Hossain, learned Advocate for the opposite party No. 1, however, pointed out that there has been some mistake in calculating the interest. In the execution petition interest has been claimed at the rate of 16% but actually the decree was passed for 13% interest. Hence we are of the opinion that the calculation as made by the opposite party No. 1 the decree-holder regarding interest at the rate of 16% be reduced to the interest at the rate of 13% and the executing Court is directed to make necessary correction regarding the rate of interest. With this modification the rule is discharged without any order as to costs.
